provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Adult buyers; the schedule and class packs are the product, teacher training is the big ticket. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vinyasa, yin, restorative, hot yoga and mat or reformer pilates explained by intensity, room heat, pace and who each suits, with a beginner-friendly marker
pageStructurePlus.why: A first-timer can't tell vinyasa from yin or mat from reformer. They book the class whose description tells them they'll be fine.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Why a private or small-group reformer intro is required before group classes, what it covers, springs and safety, price, and how to book it
pageStructurePlus.why: Reformer studios lose newcomers who book a group class and get turned away. A clear intro path keeps them and sells the first private.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Arrive early, grip socks for reformer, mat and towel rental, hydration for heated rooms, the late door policy, phones, and where to leave shoes
pageStructurePlus.why: Newcomers fear the unspoken rules of a yoga room more than the poses. Knowing them ahead gets them through the door.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The 200-hour teacher training dates, schedule, lead trainers, curriculum, tuition and payment plan, application and an info session booking
pageStructurePlus.why: Teacher training is a studio's largest single sale. Applicants compare schools for months and need every detail written down.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Upcoming inversions, breathwork and anatomy workshops, sound baths, and weekend retreats with dates, price, deposit and what's included
pageStructurePlus.why: Workshops fill the calendar and bring in people who never take a regular class. They sell on a dated page with a buy button.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Prenatal yoga and postnatal pilates by trimester and weeks after birth, doctor clearance note, baby-welcome classes and what changes in each pose
pageStructurePlus.why: Expecting and new mothers search for a studio that explicitly welcomes them, and they stay as members for years.

designDirections.name: First Class
designDirections.bestFor: Small yoga studios that need new-student bookings and a readable timetable more than a brand
designDirections.headlineSample: Yoga for every body in {City}. New student offer inside.
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach Sorbet's soft rounded type feels like an unintimidating first class, and the split hero keeps the new student button beside a calm room shot.

designDirections.name: Open Schedule
designDirections.bestFor: Busy yoga and pilates studios where the weekly schedule and class packs are the whole product
designDirections.headlineSample: Yoga and reformer pilates classes in {City}, every day
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Sky Kite's pale sky ground reads calm and open rather than childish here, and the card stack makes the day's classes the hero.

designDirections.name: Quiet Room
designDirections.bestFor: Boutique reformer pilates studios and yoga studios with teacher training and retreats
designDirections.headlineSample: Reformer pilates and yoga in {City}, by appointment
designDirections.whyItFits: Driftwood's quiet neutrals and old-style serif feel like natural wood floors and linen, and suit a boutique studio selling privates and training.

openers.line: Your yoga studio's Google listing has hours and a phone number but no website, so someone searching hot yoga in {City} can't see today's classes or the new student offer.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the yoga studio page behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Bio link to a booking app
openers.line: Your bio link goes straight into a booking app with class names and nothing about vinyasa versus yin. A first-timer wants to know which yoga class won't embarrass them.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note where it lands: a booking app, a link page or nothing.
openers.linkLine: Your yoga and pilates classes, explained before the booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: The studio site on your listing still promotes a yoga workshop from a past season. Someone choosing a pilates studio notices that before the new class schedule.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old workshop, old prices, a broken schedule widget. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Same studio, with this season's yoga and pilates: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your yoga studio site on my phone and the schedule loaded as a tiny embedded box. People check yoga times on their phone on the way out of work.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same studio, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: It's not clear anywhere whether a newcomer needs a private reformer intro before group pilates. People who book the wrong class get turned away and don't come back.
openers.hook: Check their pages for intro or private requirements on reformer. If it's missing or buried, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A reformer pilates intro path that books itself: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts of the yoga room at golden hour are lovely, and they scroll away under class reminders. A studio page would let that room do the selling.
openers.hook: Find a recent post of the room, the reformers or a sunrise class. Note what it shows.
openers.linkLine: Your yoga room, where newcomers decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews have people saying they were nervous about their first yoga class and felt welcome. Those reviews belong beside the new student offer.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about feeling welcome or being a beginner. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Beginner reviews beside the yoga and pilates booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: January is when people promise themselves a yoga practice. The studios with an intro offer and a clear beginner class grab them in the first week.
openers.hook: Use this from late November to mid-January, or late August for September. Name the moment.
openers.linkLine: A New Year yoga intro page, ready to book: {demo-link}

openers.line: People plan tomorrow's yoga class in bed the night before. Right now the studio can't answer 'is this one OK for beginners' at that hour.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking about beginners, heat or what to bring. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A yoga studio page that answers beginners at 11pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a yoga or pilates teacher to cover classes. Good instructors check the studio's site to see the class style and the community before they reply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted for teachers or front desk. Note the style or class times named.
openers.linkLine: A yoga studio page with a teach-here section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your upcoming yoga retreat is announced in a post with 'DM to reserve'. A retreat page with the deposit button would take bookings while you teach.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a workshop, retreat or teacher training. Note the dates and the event.
openers.linkLine: A yoga retreat page with deposits online: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a class pack or membership price for the yoga studio anywhere. Someone comparing studios usually starts with the one that lists the intro price.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for drop-in, pack or membership pricing. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Yoga class packs and memberships, priced plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your teachers' yoga and pilates certifications and training hours are why a careful beginner would choose the studio, and they're not shown anywhere.
openers.hook: Look for certifications or training hours in teacher bios or posts. Never invent one.
openers.linkLine: Your yoga and pilates teachers and their training: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like the studio's regulars bring their friends to class. That friend still looks the yoga studio up before buying a pack.
openers.hook: Look for 'bring a friend' posts or reviews saying 'my friend brought me'. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a regular's friend would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted looked beautiful. A workshop or community class like that should open the yoga studio's site.
openers.hook: Pick their newest workshop, retreat or special class post and name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That yoga moment, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted looked lovely.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the listing, your social pages and the booking app, but nothing that tells a beginner which yoga or pilates class to try. I put together a sample studio page with a class style guide, the schedule and the new student offer, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got lost among class bookings. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a class style and heat guide, a reformer intro path, the schedule and a teacher training page, and it sends bookings to the system you already use. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for yoga and pilates studios here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss between classes. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a class style guide, a reformer intro path and the new student offer, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and schedule or workshop updates. For a studio your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes in the quiet hour after the morning classes?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before New Year intentions kick in."

objections.objection: My booking app is my website.
objections.handler: "It sells the class pack well. It can't tell a nervous beginner that yin is gentle or that reformer needs an intro first. The site explains, then sends them into the same app."

objections.objection: Our students find us on Instagram.
objections.handler: "Instagram shows the room. The site is where a beginner checks which yoga class to take and what it costs before committing. It links back to the grid."

objections.objection: Teacher training fills itself from our students.
objections.handler: "Then the page is for the applicants who aren't students yet, and for the ones who need to show a partner the dates and tuition before they commit."

objections.objection: One of our teachers handles the website.
objections.handler: "Lovely, keep them involved. I'll hand over the style guide and workshop pages. If they'd rather teach than update it, the offer stands."
"That's when to build it. Fall and January bring the new students, and the beginner pages should be ready before they start searching."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the style guide, the intro path and the schedule. A couple of members on monthly packs cover it within the year."

email.subject: Yoga and pilates site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for yoga and pilates studios in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a beginner class guide. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} yoga studio demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — New Year is close, and beginners pick a yoga or pilates studio in the first week of January. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few members on monthly packs for a year, never to the cost of a reformer.
Sell the site as the explainer in front of their booking app. Don't quote to replace the app.
Price teacher training as its own page set. It is the studio's largest sale and deserves the most copy.
Only quote the reformer intro path for studios with reformers. Mat-only studios don't need it.
Keep monthly add-ons under one unlimited membership. Owners measure everything against it.
Sell New Year work in October and teacher training pages four to six months before the training starts.

lineItems.description: Max when every class type has intensity, heat, a beginner marker and a short video of the room.
Max with private and small-group intro options, payment, grip sock reminder and an unlock for group classes.
Max with curriculum, trainer bios, schedule, payment plan, application form and info session booking.
Max with deposits, room types for retreats, a packing list and early-bird pricing that switches off by date.
Max with classes by stage, clearance note, baby-welcome schedule and a teacher with prenatal training named.

lineItems.item: Gift card and class pack store
lineItems.description: Max with emailed and printable cards, intro packs and a holiday banner.
Max when the style guide, etiquette page, intro offer and schedule notes are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Studio light shoot of a real yoga class
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A morning class and an empty reformer room shot in natural light, only students who sign off, so the yoga studio's pages look like the real room."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a sunny morning class with a consent sign-up.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google listing upkeep for the yoga studio
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Workshops, new class times and the intro offer posted to the studio's Google listing weekly, so searches for yoga or pilates nearby show a lively studio."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after a student's fifth class
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After their fifth yoga or pilates class, a new student gets a gentle text asking for a review, once the nerves are gone and the habit has started."

whatElseYouSell.name: New Year and September intro ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for the yoga studio's intro offer in January and September, sent to the beginner style guide and paused once intro packs sell out."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October and July. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: Teacher training enrolment campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Info session invites to current students, a short email series and posts for the yoga teacher training, timed months ahead of the start date."
whatElseYouSell.when: Four to six months before the next teacher training starts.

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday class pack and gift card push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A December push for yoga class packs as gifts, on the site and in the studio, so the present is a practice instead of a candle."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run Thanksgiving to New Year.

whatElseYouSell.name: Retreat brochure and landing page
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A retreat brochure and landing page with the daily yoga schedule, rooms and deposit, ready to send to the studio's students."
whatElseYouSell.when: When they announce a retreat, six to nine months ahead.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly studio newsletter
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One calm email a month with new yoga classes, workshops and a teacher spotlight, written and sent for you."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the email list from bookings is clean.

withoutAI.route: Massage therapists and acupuncturists students see
withoutAI.whoPays: Each practitioner, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The massage therapist who rents your studio's back room needs a booking page of their own. Your students are already their clients."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wellness practitioners share clients with yoga studios and often rent space there. The studio owner's word is enough.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The retreat centre you take students to has no page for studios planning group yoga retreats. Introduce me to the owner."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Retreat venues sell to studios, and a studio that books every year is the best introduction they'll get.

withoutAI.route: Pelvic floor and prenatal physical therapists
withoutAI.whoPays: The clinic, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pelvic floor clinic that sends postnatal clients to your pilates classes needs a better site. You can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: These clinics refer to pilates studios already. A clear site helps both sides of the referral.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each doula, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The doulas who teach in your prenatal yoga community need booking pages. I'll build them on a simple, warm template."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Doulas get clients by word of mouth in exactly the studio's prenatal community.

withoutAI.route: Local yoga wear and mat makers
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The local brand whose mats and leggings sell in your studio has no proper shop page. I'd like an introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small makers rely on studio retail and trust studio owners' recommendations.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each teacher, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The touring teachers who lead workshops at your studio need a tour page with dates and booking. I'll build it so it links back to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Touring teachers need every host studio's dates in one place, and they trust the studios that host them.

withAI.route: Booking assistant for the massage therapist
withAI.pitchLine: "Clients ask about a deep tissue massage after a hard yoga week and get booked into an open slot, without a missed call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Solo practitioners can't answer the phone with hands on a client. A small fee is less than one session.

withAI.route: Group enquiry assistant for retreat venues
withAI.pitchLine: "Studio owners planning a yoga retreat ask about rooms, meals and practice space, and get answers and a date hold any time."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venue enquiries arrive across time zones. A hold request is easy to value.

withAI.route: Intake request helper for the pelvic floor clinic
withAI.pitchLine: "A postnatal pilates student requests a pelvic floor appointment at night and the clinic gets a tidy request in the morning, with no medical advice given."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clinics lose patients to unreturned calls. It only collects and books.

withAI.pitchLine: "Parents from the prenatal yoga class ask about the doula's packages and due-date availability, and get answers and a consult booking."
withAI.whyItWorks: Doulas are often at births and can't reply. One captured client pays for a year.

withAI.route: Fit and fabric helper for the yoga wear maker
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers ask which leggings stay put in hot yoga or which mat grips best, and get answers from the maker's own product notes."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fit questions stall online sales. Answering them sells more without discounting.

withAI.route: Tour date assistant for visiting teachers
withAI.pitchLine: "Students ask where the teacher's next workshop is and get the nearest host studio's date and booking link."
withAI.whyItWorks: Touring teachers get the same question in every city, and each answer sells a seat for a host studio.

softwareAI.name: Intro offer follow-up for new yoga students
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new student on the intro offer gets a welcome note, a nudge toward a second class and a membership offer before the intro yoga pass runs out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the intro offer rules, membership options and access to the booking app.

softwareAI.name: Reformer intro gate
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Group reformer pilates classes unlock only after the intro session is done, so nobody books a class they'll be turned away from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build or month 2, for reformer studios. Needs intro rules and booking app access.

softwareAI.name: Teacher training application portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Teacher training applicants apply, pay the deposit, sign up for a payment plan and get the reading list in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Four to six months before the next yoga teacher training. Needs the application questions, tuition and payment plan.

softwareAI.name: Studio message answerer for beginners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Is hot yoga OK for a beginner' and 'do I need grip socks for reformer' get answered from the studio's own guide, with a booking link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the style guide, etiquette and pricing, updated when they change. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Class pack expiry reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students with yoga classes left on a pack get a reminder before it expires, so they use it and buy the next one instead of feeling cheated."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs pack rules and booking app data.

softwareAI.name: Workshop and retreat checkout
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Workshops and yoga retreats sell with deposits, room choices and balance reminders, without a DM thread for every booking."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before the next retreat announcement. Needs dates, prices and cancellation terms.

softwareAI.name: Studio phone and voicemail assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "During a silent savasana, the studio phone still gets answered quietly elsewhere, the beginner question handled and the class booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they trust you. Needs schedule, pricing and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Substitute teacher board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A yoga teacher posts a class needing cover, qualified subs claim it, and the schedule updates without a midnight group text."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for studios with several teachers. Needs teacher list and which classes each can teach.

softwareAI.name: Yoga review reply drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Yoga and pilates reviews get a short, unhurried reply in the owner's tone, mentioning the class style, waiting in a queue to approve after the last class."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review asks. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Class theme and post writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A teacher's class theme for the week becomes a short post and newsletter paragraph in the yoga studio's voice, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs past posts and teacher themes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Private session and duet booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Private yoga and reformer pilates sessions and duets booked with a named teacher and paid as packs, so the studio sells its highest-value hour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs teacher availability and private prices.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed member welcome-back note
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students who haven't been on the mat in two months get a warm note with a returning-student pack, timed before January and September."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs visit history from the booking app.

softwareAI.name: Beginner class matcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A newcomer shares their fitness, injuries and what they're after, and the matcher suggests the right yoga or pilates class and books it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the owner's placement rules. Never gives medical advice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Teacher training quiz companion
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Trainees quiz themselves on anatomy, sequencing and Sanskrit names from the yoga studio's own training manual, between weekends."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, before the next training cohort. Needs the training manual and lead trainer approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Teacher pay per class report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each yoga teacher's classes, headcounts and per-head bonuses added up for payroll, with privates and workshops included."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for studios paying per class or per head. Needs pay rules and booking data.

softwareAI.name: Studio retail and mat rental tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Grip socks, mats and towels sold or rented at the yoga studio front desk, with a reorder list before the sock basket runs empty."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, if they sell retail. Needs product list and prices.

softwareAI.name: Workshop waitlist release
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a full workshop or reformer class gets a cancellation, the next person on the waitlist gets a text and the spot is theirs to claim."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs waitlist access in the booking app.

softwareAI.name: Schedule gap and class fill analysis
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month the owner sees which yoga and pilates time slots run half-empty and which turn people away, with suggested schedule swaps."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, after months of booking data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: On-demand class library
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members stream a recorded yoga or mat pilates class from the studio when they travel, as part of their membership or as an add-on."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs recorded classes and teacher consent.

softwareAI.name: Retreat itinerary and packing assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Retreat guests ask about flights, the daily yoga schedule and what to pack, and get answers from the retreat packet any time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once a retreat is booked. Needs the retreat packet. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the style guide and reformer intro gate for boutique studios
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Yoga and pilates studios, monthly per studio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a beginner style guide and a reformer intro gate in front of one studio's booking app. Every boutique pilates studio loses newcomers the same way."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Studios run on a few booking apps, so one integration serves many. Owners trade notes in teacher circles.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Yoga teacher registry and school directory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Students look for a registered yoga school near them. A directory with each school's training dates and an apply button sends them straight in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Registries earn from school membership. Showing that registration brings applicants makes renewals easy.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your reformers are in studios all over the region. A find-a-studio map of your customers, with intro booking links, keeps them buying from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Equipment makers compete for studio loyalty, and studios happily appear on a map that sends them students.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each reformer pilates location needs its own schedule, intro path and teacher page on one shared template. I've built the pattern."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes every location, and franchisors roll out what works.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets yoga clients and rebuilds the same class guide every time. License my studio template with the style guide and teacher training pages built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the relationship; you sell the yoga-specific structure you already proved.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You run several yoga retreats a year with deposits, rooms and waitlists in spreadsheets. One booking platform for the season fixes that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retreat companies run the same model repeatedly, and every host studio sees the result.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your staff wellness budget could buy lunchtime yoga at local studios. A sign-up page listing participating studios and class times makes it simple."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Employers want uptake they can count, and the studio client is the first participating studio.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior living chair yoga and mobility classes
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your residents' chair yoga and gentle pilates classes, run by local teachers, need a schedule families can see and a sign-up for residents."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Senior communities market activities to families. The studio client often supplies the teacher.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each studio, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Barre and meditation studios sell class packs to the same students as yoga, with the same beginner fears. I take the template to them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The booking-first pattern carries over, and the yoga site is proof they can try.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Guests want sunrise yoga at your resort. A class schedule and booking page for the local teachers you contract makes it a sellable amenity."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Resorts contract local studios for classes, and the studio client is the introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New yoga and pilates studios elsewhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "After one reformer and hot yoga studio in {City} runs on it, the same intro path and style guide go to studios in towns that never compete with it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything, including the finished studio proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue a messy booking app switch
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Moving booking apps broke your class pack links and intro offer. I can reconnect the studio site and the packs, having done it for another studio."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Studios mid-switch lose bookings daily and will pay to stop it.

upsellLadder.offer: Yoga studio site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The yoga studio site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new workshop is a message to me, not an evening at the laptop."

upsellLadder.trigger: A newcomer books a group reformer class without the intro and has to be turned away.
upsellLadder.line: "That newcomer turned away from reformer is exactly what an intro gate prevents."

upsellLadder.offer: Intro offer follow-up and review asks
upsellLadder.trigger: A month of intro offers shows students who took one or two yoga classes and stopped.
upsellLadder.line: "Those intro students liked the room. A welcome note and a second-class nudge brings more of them back."

upsellLadder.trigger: They announce a workshop or retreat with 'DM to reserve'.
upsellLadder.line: "Let the yoga retreat take deposits online while you teach, instead of a DM thread per guest."

upsellLadder.trigger: They say the same beginner and grip sock questions fill their evenings.
upsellLadder.line: "Those 'is this OK for a beginner' messages get answered from your guide while you rest."

upsellLadder.offer: Teacher training application portal and campaign
upsellLadder.trigger: They set dates for the next yoga teacher training.
upsellLadder.line: "Teacher training is your biggest sale. Let's give applicants a proper portal and invite them months ahead."

upsellLadder.offer: New Year and September intro ads
upsellLadder.trigger: It's October and the January beginner classes have room.
upsellLadder.line: "New Year yoga beginners are about to search. Let's point ads at the style guide before they do."

upsellLadder.trigger: They come back from a retreat and mention the venue's clunky booking.
upsellLadder.line: "The retreat venue you love has no page for studios. Would you introduce me?"
